name_note: GTDB places this species in the split genus Blautia_A; the literature and NCBI name is Blautia wexlerae.

sentences.text: Blautia wexlerae was described from human faeces as a Gram-positive, anaerobic, non-sporulating coccobacillus that produces acetate and succinate.
Species of Blautia are typical inhabitants of the human gut, and this one carries most Wood-Ljungdahl pathway genes yet does not grow on hydrogen plus carbon dioxide.
It was counted in faeces of twelve healthy Japanese subjects using real-time PCR primers specific for this species and Blautia luti.
A review describes it as a strong candidate next-generation probiotic and collects the food factors reported to change its abundance.
